findings.name: stand-in
findings.detail: The onboarding drive uses the fixture answer set (data/onboarding.json) as the employee's own answers and confirmation; that is a named stand-in for the employee's device taps. The state machine, validation and gate are the product's own code, and the confirmation gate still refuses a non-employee confirmer by construction (suite/onboarding/src/protocol.js confirm()).

findings.name: stub-turn route
findings.detail: On this install the deterministic stub route (`stub-turn`, provider fleet-selftest-stub) returned status=completed with provider_calls=0 and empty assistant text for 2/2 probes: the turn machinery starts a session but no model turn is produced. The stub route therefore does NOT stand in for a model-quality answer here; the model leg is named PENDING below.

pending: provider credential for the fleet profile (owner act): the assistant's model-quality role answer and the model-conducted onboarding conversation cannot run. The deterministic stub route produced no provider call on this install (stub-turn probes recorded). What ran instead: fixture assistant records, onboarding to `active` through the product protocol with fixture answers (stand-in for the employee's own words), and one real fleet agent session per cast member.
